name: Autonomous Parking Operations
tagline: Keep a busy facility stable while capacity changes.
brief: Adapt to arrival surges, closures, charging failures, lane pressure, and gate outages.
context: Incidents happen while the controller is running; inbound assignments may need to change before a car reaches its bay.
narrative:
ParkFlow now serves airport and event traffic. Arrival volume changes quickly, spaces close for maintenance, and exit gates can fail while bays remain occupied.

Shared lanes create back-pressure: too many simultaneous movements slow future work. Priority vehicles may move ahead, but ordinary vehicles must not wait forever. Hard category violations are never allowed; compatible fallbacks are allowed with a service penalty.
objective: Recover from every visible incident, preserve safety, prevent starvation, and pass the hidden capacity and surge scenarios.
learningObjective: Balance throughput, service priority, fairness, category preservation, and recovery under load.
intelligenceExplanation:
The interview starts with no rules. Build the flow around live queue pressure, patience, lane load, gate availability, and hard eligibility.

The policy must keep making progress as capacity closes and recovers instead of repeatedly starting movements that the facility cannot support.
hint: Treat exits as capacity recovery, compatibility as a hard filter, and VIP/EV placement as preferences. Use waiting time to prevent starvation.
hints: When the exit queue grows, each waiting departure is also an unavailable bay.
A closed preferred category may recover later, but the head vehicle's patience determines whether waiting is defensible.
Avoid reacting to congestion by continuously starting more entry movements.
